end.summary:
Rohan showed understanding of food miles as the full journey from farm to home and found 42 km by adding 30 and 12.
They practised comparing distances and linking longer journeys with more fuel and pollution; this is still not steady and needs checking with new examples.
They practised ways to reduce food miles, including choosing local and seasonal food; limits and reasons need checking next time.
The idea that imported or distant food is more special or nutritious appeared again and was not corrected by the last time it appeared.
end.parentNote: Asha practised food miles using whole-journey examples, and Rohan used addition and truck-distance reasoning to discuss fuel and pollution. They also identified local, seasonal mangoes and refrigeration as relevant factors. Rohan continued to mix up distance with food quality or nutrition, and this was not corrected after the last example. At home, compare two foods by asking where each came from, what transport or storage it needed, and whether distance proves quality.
